clauses.text:
I hereby establish the following regulations
for the Canal Zone.,~
Section I. The Chief Health Officer of The Panama Canal, under the
direction of the Governor of The Panama Canal, is hereby authorized and
directed to administer the regulations established hereunder; and hie may
designate one or more assistants to aid him in the performance of his duties,
who shall exercise such powers as the Chief Health Qfficer may delegate to them
from time to time.

clauses.label: Section 2.

source.page_or_item: ProQuest Congressional Replica of Original, file PT1-1920-EO-3210.pdf (3 pages)

clauses.text:
Section 2. In conformity with Section I, "Title II, of the above mentioned
Act of Congress, the word "liquor" wvhen used in these regulations, shall be
construed to include alcohol, brandy, whiskey, rumn, gin, beer, ale, porter and
wine, and in addition thereto any spirituous, vinous, malt, or freinented liquors,
iquids and compounds, whether medicated, proprietary, patented or not, and
by whatever name called, containing one-half of onc per cent or more of alcohol
by volume, which are fit for use for beverage pur, cases ; Provided, that the fore-
going definition shall not extend to dealcoholized wine or to any beverage or
liquid produced by the process by which beer, ale, porter or wine is produced,
if it contain less than one-half of one per cent of alcohol by volume, and is
otherwise denominated than as beer, ale, or porter.
In conformity with Section a, Title III of the above mientionedl Act of
Congress, the term " alcohol " means that substance known ats ethyl alcohol,
hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirit of wine, from whatever source or whatever
processes produced,

Section 5. No one but a physician, authorized to do so under the preceding
section, shall be permitted to prescribe liquors for medicinal purposes in the
Canal Zone, and no liquors shall be so prescribed except after careful physical
examination of the person for whose use such prescription is sought, or if such
examination is found impracticable, then only when -upon the best information
obtainable the physician believes that the issue of such liquor to such person
is necessary and will afford himt relief from sonmc known ailment. A prescription
issued bona fide under these regulations shall authorize the person named in
the same to use and possess the liquor described in the prescription, and in the
quantity and for the time therein stated,

regulations shall be punished by a tine of not more than $i,ooo and imprison.

the District Court of the Canal Zone.
